blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Sketching is one of the most natural ways for people to express visual ideas. Unlike the text prompts that most generative systems rely on today, a sketch captures spatial structure and intent directly, including where a designer wants highlights and shadows to appear. Yet current sketch-to-3D pipelines have no input for that intent: they bake the drawn shading into the texture as dark paint, and the light cannot be moved. We propose a system that transforms a rough garment sketch, marked with sparse annotations (a star for a highlight and a moon for a shadow), and a short text prompt describing the texture, into a textured 3D mesh with an explicit directional light, as a scene that can be relit and edited after generation. The two symbols are the most frequent proposals in an elicitation study with art students. From the marked sketch the system predicts the scene's directional light and, separately, a displacement field that bends the surface so that the moon-marked regions fall into shadow under that light, rather than being painted dark in the texture.

blocks.en: 2.1 Sketch-based modeling
blocks.zh: 2.1 以速记为基础的建模

blocks.en:
Early interactive systems read strokes as geometric operations: Teddy [ IMT99 ] inflates a closed contour into a freeform
surface, and FiberMesh [ NISA07 ] keeps the drawn curves
as editable handles on the result. Structured annotations [ GIZ09 ] let the user place primitives and
constraints, such as symmetry and equal length, on a 2D drawing to settle
its 3D interpretation. Garments have their own line of work, because a
drawn garment is defined relative to a body. Turquin et
al. [ TWB+07 ] lift contours drawn over a view of a 3D body
model into a garment around it, and FoldSketch [ LSGV18 ] lets a designer draw fold strokes on an existing garment and solves for a
sewing pattern that physically reproduces them.

blocks.en: 2.2 Specifying lighting
blocks.zh: 2.2 指定照明

blocks.en:
Our marks specify lighting on a drawing, so we look at how light is
handled in two settings: how artists draw it, by showing where it falls
and where shadows form, and how 3D tools set it, as an object the user
can move and edit.
blocks.zh:
我们的标记在图纸上指定了照明, 所以我们看看光是如何的
在两种情况下处理:艺术家如何绘制,显示其落地
和阴影在哪里形成,以及3D工具如何设置它,作为用户的对象
可移动并编辑。

blocks.en:
Artists usually draw light through what it does to a form. Painting manuals teach a small vocabulary of
shading events on a form: the highlight, the terminator where the surface
turns away from the light, the core shadow beyond it, and the cast shadow [ Gur10 ] . Non-photorealistic rendering reproduces these
conventions from 3D, placing hatching according to a known light [ HZ00 ] ; there the light is an input. Our
elicitation (Sec. 3.2 ) asks a different question:
which symbols people would use to indicate where light and shadow fall.
blocks.zh:

在形式上阴影事件:亮点,表面的终结者
远离光明 超越它的核心阴影 和被抛出阴影 [Gur10]. 非相片现实主义渲染 复制这些
3D的常规,按照已知的光[HZ00]放入孵化;其中光是输入. 我们
诱导(第3.2条)提出了另一个问题:
哪些符号是人们用来表示光和阴影落下的地方。

blocks.en:
3D tools instead expose the light source itself. Blender, for example, exposes light as an explicit
object, such as a point, spot, area or directional (sun) source, whose
orientation, color and intensity the artist edits in the viewport [ Ble24 ] , and glTF carries the same parameters between
tools [ Khr18 ] . Light is then editable after the fact, but
the user must reason about causes: to put a highlight in a chosen place,
the artist moves the source and watches the result. Some research methods remove this step: the user specifies the effect,
such as a highlight or a painted target, and the method solves for the light [ OMSI07 , Pel10 ] . Poulin and Fournier [ PF92 ] recover light positions from highlights and shadows sketched onto a
rendered scene, and Pellacini et al. [ PBMF07 ] solve
for light parameters that reproduce a painted target illumination;
Schmidt et al. [ SPN+16 ] survey the wider space. Our marks
are closest to Poulin and Fournier’s highlight and shadow sketches. These
methods, however, operate on an existing 3D scene, where each candidate
light can be rendered and compared with the user’s target. In our setting there is no scene yet, only a drawing, so the light has to be inferred before any geometry exists.

blocks.en: 2.3 Text- and image-conditioned 3D generation
blocks.zh: 2.3 有文字和图像条件的3D生成

blocks.en:
Current 3D generators work feed-forward. Novel-view diffusion and large
reconstruction models lift a single image to a mesh in seconds [ LWVH+23 , HZG+24 ] , and native 3D latent generators such
as TRELLIS [ XLX+25 ] and Hunyuan3D [ Hun25 ] produce high-quality geometry, textured by
a separate multi-view painting stage. Commercial services such as Meshy [ Mes25 ] put the same pipeline behind a text or image prompt.
blocks.zh:
目前的三维发电机工作向前进。 小说视图传播和大型
重建模型在秒内将单个图像提升到网格[LWVH+23,HZG+24],以及本地3D潜在生成器等
作为TRELLIS [XLX+25] 和Hunyuan3D [Hun25] 生产出高质量的几何学,纹理由
一个单独的多视图绘画舞台。 Meshy [Mes25]等商业服务将同样的管道放在文本或图像提示后.

blocks.en:
For our purposes these systems share two properties. First, their
control channels are text and images, so shading can only be
specified by handing them a picture that already contains it. Second, they return geometry and material but no light.
Recent texture stages output physically based materials instead of a single color map [ Hun25 ] , so their assets can be
relit in principle. However, the illumination of the conditioning image
is treated as a nuisance and removed from the albedo [ ZCQ+24 ] ; where removal is incomplete, it stays in the
texture. Either way, the output carries no light of its own, and any lighting
left in the texture cannot be moved. We use such a generator to build the mesh and paint its texture, and
add the light as a separate element of the scene.
blocks.zh:
为了我们的目的,这些系统有两个特性。 首先,他们
控制通道是文本和图像,所以阴影只能是
指定,将已经包含的图片交给他们。 第二,它们返回几何和材料,但没有光.
最近的纹理相输出基于物理的材料,而不是一个单一的颜色图[Hun25],所以它们的资产可以是
原则上重新表述。 然而,调制图像的发光
被作为烦恼对待,从反照率中取出[ZCQ+24];如果清除不完整,则留在
纹理。 不管怎样,输出没有它自己的光 和任何照明
无法被移动。 我们用这种发电机来制造网状并涂上它的纹理,
添加光作为场景的一个单独元素.

This section introduces the shading marks, the input that separates our
system from other sketch-to-3D pipelines. We first set out what the
notation must achieve (Sec. 3.1 ), then
describe the study we used to choose the symbols
(Sec. 3.2 ), and finally define what each symbol means
and how it is placed (Sec. 3.3 ).

blocks.en: 3.1 Motivation
blocks.zh: 3.1 动机

blocks.en:
Our goal is to let a designer say, directly on the sketch, how the
garment should be lit: where light falls and where the fabric should
be in shadow. For such marks to be useful, they need two
properties. A designer without training in shading should be able to
make them and to guess what each one means without being taught. Both
depend on the symbols themselves, so instead of inventing symbols
we asked people which ones they would use (Sec. 3.2 ).

衣服应该被点燃:灯光落下的地方和布料应该在哪里
在阴影中。 这些标记要有用,就需要两个
属性。 未受过阴影培训的设计者应当能够
让他们猜自己是干什么的 却不教别人 两者
取决于符号本身,所以不是发明符号
我们问人们,他们会使用哪些(第3.2节)。

blocks.en: 3.2 Elicitation
blocks.zh: 3.2 说 明

blocks.en:
To choose the symbols, we asked art students which symbols they would
use to mark a highlight and a shadow. We first describe the
questionnaire and how the drawn answers were coded, then report which
symbols were proposed most often and how the two categories differed.
blocks.zh:
为了选择符号,我们问艺术学生 他们会选择哪些符号
用于标记亮点和阴影。 我们首先描述
以及如何编码所抽取的答复,然后报告
人们最经常提出这两个类别的符号,以及这两个类别有何不同。

blocks.en:
We ran an elicitation study [ WARM05 , WMW09 ] with 28 art students at our university in April 2026. The study was introduced in an information session during class, and participation was
voluntary. Participants completed a paper questionnaire: two background
items (drawing experience and formal training in light and shading), a
free drawing task, two items on how they had depicted highlights and
shadows, and the target item: “If you had to encode shading using ONLY symbols, what would you
choose? Fill one symbol per category: Highlight: ___ , Shadow: ___” .
Answers were free-form drawings. Most participants were novices: 18
described themselves as beginners with no formal training, 8 as
intermediate and 2 as advanced, and 5 of 28 had studied light and shading
formally.

The U-Net [ RFB15 ] takes the marked sketch as its

irradiance map. To

made white and matte, which leaves only the light that reaches each
point, shadows included.

Sec. 4.6 , it forms the displacement field that

training sketches we draw without moons, where it is supervised to

target is rescaled per garment, so the prediction ranks crease

blocks.en:
Surface color is produced by FLUX.1 [ Bla24 ] with a ControlNet [ ZRA23 , Sha24 ] that conditions it
on the clean sketch and the text prompt. Because a sketch carries no
color, the prompt is the only input that specifies it. What the
branch has to produce is base color without the scene’s illumination,
so that the predicted irradiance can be applied afterwards rather
than being baked into the color. A pretrained image generator does not do this by default, since it is
trained to produce lit, shaded pictures. We therefore train two parts of the ControlNet and leave both it and
FLUX otherwise frozen: a rank- 64 64 LoRA adapter [ HSW+22 ] on
its attention and MLP layers, 69 69 M parameters, and the output layers
of its double-stream blocks, the last stage before it passes its
signal to FLUX, 47 47 M.

percentile of its magnitude, so it sits in proportion to the folds

one: inside its footprint we keep whichever is larger, the crest or
the predicted field. The predicted light sets which side of the mark
the crest sits on; its footprint and its distance from the mark are

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We have presented a system that reads the star and moon marks a designer places on a garment sketch and returns a 3D scene in which the light is an explicit, editable source
and the shadows the marks ask for are made by displacing the surface. Two marks, a
star where light falls and a moon where the garment should be in
shadow, came out of an elicitation study with art students and are
stamped on the sketch itself. From the marked sketch and a text
prompt, the network predicts the light’s direction and where the
fabric should fold, recovering the light direction to 22.9 ∘ 22.9^{\circ} against 47.5 ∘ 47.5^{\circ} for the best fixed direction fitted on the
training split. Displacing the surface darkens 79 % 79\% of the moon
marks on held-out renders, and 86 % 86\% on renders we mark ourselves on
flat cloth, where the reconstruction offers no fold to deepen.

One part remains open. The crest beside each mark takes its height
from the predicted field and its side from the predicted light, but
its footprint and its distance from the mark are fixed by a rule.
Predicting those is our next step.
